evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: entry / form and historical dictionary references
evidence.text: The entry says 爸 is not recorded in Shuowen; describes the modern graph as 父 above 巴; and cites the Ji Yun definition 爸, 爹、父也. It lists image records for Yu Pian, Guangyun, Ji Yun, Zihui, Zhengzitong and Kangxi, but the page text does not date the first attestation itself.
evidence.title: 爸 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: 廣雅 via 識典古籍
evidence.text: The entry groups 爸 with 爹 and 㸙 and glosses them as father. The modern research article consulted below identifies this as an early record in the Three Kingdoms era. This is lexical evidence for the father term, not an account of how the graph was formed.
evidence.title: 釋親-廣雅全文原文-識典古籍

evidence.source: Deng Li and Huang Renxuan, Language Research (2026)
evidence.text: The article reports 爸 as a later graph, absent from Shuowen, and cites Guangya (dated by the article to the Three Kingdoms period) 爸，父也; Yu Pian 蒲可切，父也; Guangyun 捕可切，父也; and Ji Yun readings 部可切 ‘爸、爹，父也’ and 必駕切 ‘Wu speakers call father 爸’. It separately dates the colloquial reduplicated form 爸爸 and 阿爸 to Qing texts, while noting the Tang form 郎爸/郎罷 in 顧況’s poem 囝. Its authors argue the father word is phonologically from 父; that is a scholarly interpretation, distinct from the graph’s component analysis.
evidence.title: 现代汉语“父亲”称谓系统音义关系研究

evidence.text: Reports a phono-semantic analysis: semantic 父 ‘father’ plus phonetic 巴. In Zhengzhang’s Old Chinese reconstruction system it gives 巴 *praː and 爸 readings *praːs and *baʔ. This supports a proposed sound-component relationship within 爸, not whole-character borrowing. The entry does not establish 巴’s original depicted object or independently recover its name.
evidence.title: 爸 - Wiktionary

evidence.text: Lists Standard Mandarin Pinyin bà, Chengdu Sichuanese Pinyin ba with tone 2, Guangzhou–Hong Kong Jyutping baa1 or baa1-4, Sixian Hakka PFS pâ, Fuzhou Bàng-uâ-cê bă/bâ, and several Southern Min forms. These are readings of 爸; they do not all instantiate the same tone or onset history.
evidence.title: 爸 - Wiktionary

evidence.text: For the father reading, the page gives Middle Chinese Baxter bjuX and Old Chinese Baxter–Sagart *[N-p](r)aʔ and Zhengzhang *baʔ. Its discussion says standard Mandarin 父 fù underwent a different modern onset development than colloquial 爸 bà. The reconstructions belong to distinct systems and should not be conflated.
evidence.title: 父 - Wiktionary

evidence.field: historical dictionary gloss and competing account
evidence.text: The Kangxi entry transmits Yu Pian 蒲可切, Guangyun 捕可切 and Ji Yun 部可切, glossing 爸 as 父也; it also cites Zhengzitong’s account that ‘barbarian languages’ called an elder 八八 or 巴巴 and that 父 was later added to make 爸, and a Ji Yun note that Wu speakers called father 爸 with reading 必駕切. This is a historical lexicographic explanation, not independently verified linguistic evidence for the proposed source language or borrowing chronology.
evidence.title: 康熙字典網上版, page 690

evidence.text: The database provides an oracle-bone record and a small-seal form and summarizes the Shuowen interpretation of 巴 as an elephant-swallowing giant snake with a very large mouth. The inspected page gives no sequence of readable intermediate forms in its text. The Shuowen interpretation is a historical account, not conclusive proof of the graph’s original referent.
evidence.title: 漢字「巴」：字形演變

evidence.source: CASE 報科學, National Taiwan University
evidence.text: The article reviews disagreements over oracle-bone forms traditionally read 巴. It argues their shapes differ from the oracle-bone snake graph 它 and notes that early textual occurrences of 巴 are chiefly place, polity or group names; it disputes taking 巴蛇 in Shanhaijing as proof that 巴 itself meant snake. It presents a kneeling-person-with-arms interpretation as a proposal, while acknowledging that identification of the graph and its development into later forms remain debated and that a Western Zhou link is missing. This is a modern argument, not a settled paleographic consensus.
evidence.title: 曾被釋為「巴」的甲骨文字與《說文解字》裡的「巴蛇食象」

evidence.text: The inspected online Shuowen section includes the account that 巴蛇食象 (‘the Ba snake eats an elephant’). This establishes that the transmitted Shuowen tradition linked 巴 and a snake story; it does not independently validate the proposed original pictorial meaning.
evidence.title: 巴部 - 說文解字在線查詢

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The related 父 entry gives the Shuowen explanation: ‘the family head who leads and teaches; from 又 holding a staff.’ This is relevant to the semantic component’s inherited graph and Shuowen interpretation, but does not date the formation of 爸.
evidence.title: 父 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.text: The page calls 爸 a colloquial form of 父 for ‘father’ and reports a proposed Proto-Sino-Tibetan source *p/ba ‘male; father’. This is a lexical-origin assertion, not evidence that 爸 as a graph was borrowed whole. Independent substantiation and a dated path for the Proto-Sino-Tibetan proposal were not established in this research.
evidence.title: 爸 - Wiktionary

gaps: No attested early manuscript or excavated occurrence of 爸 itself was visually inspected. The consulted 2026 study reports a Three Kingdoms-era Guangya attestation, but this research did not establish a dated physical witness for that graph.
The phonetic classification 父 + 巴 is a source-reported analysis; no early 爸 inscription or independently inspected glyph sequence demonstrates when the compound was formed.

The origin and original depicted referent of 巴 remain disputed. The proposed animal/giant-snake reading and alternative human-figure readings are not settled; therefore the depicted object's name and pronunciation cannot be independently reconstructed here to prove a sound match.

The association of the colloquial father word with Proto-Sino-Tibetan *p/ba, and the argument that 爸 preserves an older pronunciation of 父, are source assertions requiring specialist corroboration. The distinct reconstructions supplied use different systems and readings.

The Kangxi mirror page carrying the actual scanned entry was not text-accessible in the opened result; the entry wording was taken from a separate search-result mirror and corroborated in part by the Ministry dictionary’s cited bibliographic records.

No claim of graphic corruption or a dated sequence from oracle-bone through seal forms to 爸 is supported by the inspected evidence. The Ministry states that 爸 is absent from Shuowen; its online image references are records, not inspected glyph images.

For 巴’s component-level relation inside 爸, no distinct origin_form is asserted: 巴 is the component shape itself. Its own deeper origin is uncertain and is not transferred to 爸 as an ancestor classification.
